sections.title: The letter double vé
paragraphs: The letter is called (double vé) /dublə ve/. Its main sound appears in (wagon) /va.ɡɔ̃/, which means railway carriage. This letter makes two sounds in French. Both sounds depend on where the word comes from originally. Most words with this letter are borrowed from other languages.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your top teeth lightly on your bottom lip. Push air out gently and turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel your voice shake. For the second sound, make a tight circle with your lips. Pull your tongue back and turn your voice on, letting air flow out.

sections.title: Spelling and sounds
paragraphs: In older borrowed words, mostly from Germanic roots, the letter sounds like a voiced consonant. You hear this sound in (wagon) /va.ɡɔ̃/. In modern loanwords, mostly from English, the letter sounds like a semivowel. A semivowel is a short sound that acts like a consonant. You hear this glide in (web) /wɛb/.

sections.title: Mistakes to avoid
paragraphs: Do not confuse the two sounds of this letter. When an older French word needs a voiced consonant, do not use the glide from wet. Say it cleanly with your top teeth on your bottom lip, like very. In modern loanwords, do not use teeth at all. Round your lips into a tight circle, exactly like win.
